dispositions.topic_text: Required coverage for round-tripping every query-significant stored value
Definition and scope of URL preservation when inserting the stored query value
dispositions.what: Whether a link keeps its query value by meaning (the decoded value equals the stored one) or by one exact serialisation; every option keeps the value one whole parameter value, the link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged.
keeps:
1. The owner interface renders every stored value as text: escaped for the
   place it appears in, never as markup or script, whoever wrote it.
options: Compare parsed element, attribute and decoded query values with the original while asserting that no structure was injected.
Require context-specific URL-component encoding followed by HTML-attribute encoding for query values.
Contract an exact serialized entity and percent-encoding spelling.
consequences: Semantic comparison permits equivalent safe encodings.
Context-specific encoding prevents a value from changing the path, origin, scheme, parameters or HTML structure.
Exact serialization unnecessarily makes one safe encoder's spelling contractual.

dispositions.topic_text: Store comparison boundary for unchanged-state testing
dispositions.what: What the bound check compares to show the store unchanged beyond the records an accepted create writes: domain records, the physical store or a generated list; every option keeps 'nothing else written'.
keeps:
A value a caller gives only ever fills a value place of a query or command
   whose structure the release fixes; it never becomes an identifier, an
   operator or syntax.
options: Compare specified domain records and effects while permitting hidden backend bookkeeping required to implement them.
Compare every physical record byte for byte except the newly inserted records.
Compare a declared allowlist of domain and bookkeeping changes supplied by the generated persistence design.
consequences: A domain-level comparison preserves backend freedom but must still prove that the input was never interpreted.
A physical comparison can reject safe implementations because indexes, counters or idempotency metadata change.
A generated allowlist gives precise physical coverage but couples the check to the persistence design.
